metadata.name: DocuMind Retrieval Evaluation Benchmark
metadata.description: Benchmark queries and ground-truth chunk relevance labels for evaluating DocuMind retrieval quality (Precision@K, Recall@K, MRR). NOTE: Entries in this template dataset contain placeholder chunk IDs. Real authoritative evaluation requires indexing a target PDF document and annotating ground-truth relevant chunk IDs from that document.

queries.question: What optimizer and learning rate were used for training the model?
queries.reference_answer: Model training was conducted using the SGD optimizer (Stochastic Gradient Descent) with an initial learning rate of 0.01, momentum of 0.9, and a cosine annealing schedule across 100 epochs.

queries.question: What is the primary architectural difference between Model A and Model B?
queries.reference_answer: Model A utilizes standard dense self-attention, whereas Model B adopts linear causal attention with flash-attention kernel dispatch, providing sub-quadratic memory scaling.

queries.question: What baseline datasets were used to evaluate benchmark accuracy?
queries.reference_answer: The authors evaluated benchmark accuracy on GLUE, SuperGLUE, and SQuAD 2.0 question answering datasets.

queries.question: What hardware specifications and GPU cluster were used for the experiment?
queries.reference_answer: All experimental evaluations were executed on a distributed cluster of 8 NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPUs with 80GB VRAM each, interconnected via 400 Gbps InfiniBand.

queries.question: What limitations and future directions did the authors outline?
queries.reference_answer: Key limitations include reliance on digital text extraction without OCR for scanned pages, with future directions focusing on exploring multi-vector ColBERT indexing.
